summary: Detector fired on gross size and cancel ratio. The tape shows a PEGGED execution algo refreshing symmetric bid and ask child orders of two parents at typical size (2071), at the touch, with cancels following the touch. No single order reached 3x depth, price did not move in the trader's favour, and there was no reversion. The 2-tick round trip is spread earned between its own bid and ask executions. Algorithmic re-pricing is supported, and neither core feature is present.

Prop trader placed three BUY limits of 4,418 each (13,254 total, 5.56x depth) 2 ticks off the touch over about 20s, sold 662 at 11:10:02.280, and all BUY orders were cancelled at 11:10:03.280 in the same millisecond as a recorded intraday-loss-limit kill switch. The cancels were a risk-system action, not a trader decision. The sell shows no reversion after the cancel, so there is no feature (b) benefit as the procedure defines it. Closing as FP on the risk-cancellation explanation, with moderate confidence because the size, one-sidedness and OTR 7 vs typical 4 are atypical.

The large BUY 17456 (7.14x depth) is an ICEBERG order that was genuinely executing. 6709 (38.4%) filled before the trader's only opposite-side trade, a SELL of 436 under a different parent order. There was no reversion after the cancel, so no benefit is shown. Both core features are absent and genuine execution is supported, so I propose closing it as a false positive.

Pegged two-sided execution algo re-pricing child orders of two parents (B and S). Cancels are symmetric (0.99) and each cancel is followed within milliseconds by a re-quote. No single order reaches 3x depth (max 0.85x). There was no favourable price move (0.0) and no reversion. The one opposite-side fill (518) and one small same-side fill (70) look like third parties hitting resting quotes. The detector fired on gross size and on cancels of the resting orders, which is the algo's normal refresh cycle. No feature (a) or (b).

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) quoting a 3819 SELL and a 763 BUY in pairs, cancelled together and re-quoted within ~10 ms, following the touch down from 9996 to 9990. The only executions were on its own SELL quotes (12207 filled), and the BUY side never executed. There is no opposite-side execution, so no benefit. No single order reached 3x depth. Closed as market making.

PROP trader placed three one-sided BUY limit layers (3 x 4,876 = 14,628, about 6x average depth) 6 ticks from the touch. None filled. About 600 ms after a market SELL (863 filled) all three were cancelled together. Feature (b) is not shown: price fell 3 ticks, there was no reversion, and the round trip was -6.1 ticks. Feature (a) is not excluded: the layers were huge, one-sided, far from the touch and never executed. No accepted explanation is supported (not a market maker, no event, no risk event, no parent or peg). A stop-out reading is only partly supported, so the evidence is mixed and I escalate to Level 2.

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) re-quoting a two-sided bid/ask pair at its typical size of 2661, about 1.14x depth. The pair is cancelled and replaced together every 2-3 s, so cancel_symmetry is 0.98. There is no single large order, no favourable price move (0.0) and no reversion (0.0). The alert is the naive detector reacting to routine quote refreshes, which it read as one-sided cancels after fills. Feature (a) is absent because the orders are quotes. Feature (b) is absent because no price moved in the trader's favour. Close as market making.

Registered SYN.A market maker (ETF-MM) quoting both sides at its typical 2853 size, re-quoting every 2-3s with bid and ask cancelled together. Cancel symmetry 0.98, max resting size 1.22x depth (no order reached 3x), price moved -1 tick against the opposite-side fills, round trip -0.21 ticks, no reversion. Neither the unintended-to-execute order nor the benefit is shown. The detector fired on gross two-sided quote turnover.

No single order reached 3x depth, price_move_ticks is 0 and reversion is 0, so there is no benefit from an opposite-side execution. The detector fired on gross submitted size and cancel volume, which is what quote refreshes produce. Closing as market making.

The detector fired on gross size versus depth and on the cancel of one side right after a fill on the other, which is what paired re-quoting looks like. Closing as market making.

Detector fired on gross size and BUY executions followed by cancels on SELL. The tape shows a pegged two-sided execution algo. All 74 orders are PEGGED children of two parents (one BUY, one SELL), each sized 2298 (about 1x depth, the trader's typical size). Cancels and re-posts are symmetric across sides (0.99) and follow the touch. The BUY side was genuinely executing (2391 filled before any opposite-side trade). No order reached 3x depth. Price moved against the opposite-side (SELL) fills, with no reversion. No feature (a) or (b) is present, so I propose closing as a false positive.

It happened once in the session, so I propose ESCALATE rather than a STOR draft. Level 2 decides.

PROP trader (no MM registration) bought 979 by market order at 10006-10007, then placed three one-sided BUY limits of 3526 each (10578 total, 4.5x depth) at 9997-9998, 5-6 ticks below the touch, with no fills. About 14s later the trader sold 979 at market at 10000. All three bids were cancelled together 600 ms later. Feature (a) is present on the resting side: large, one-sided, away from the touch, never executed, cancel_symmetry 0. Feature (b) is not shown: the price fell 3 ticks, there was no favourable move, no reversion and a negative round trip. The sale looks like a loss-making exit, but that does not explain why the bids were placed and then pulled at the sale. No legitimate explanation is supported, so the evidence is mixed and I escalate. I am not proposing a STOR draft because there is no repetition and no benefit.

The price moved against the trader after that fill (-1 tick) and did not revert. No single order reached 3x depth. No spoofing features found, and algorithmic re-pricing is supported.

The same-side executions came after the opposite-side fills, but they were small (914, share 0.9%), and the two-sided structure means that sequence says nothing about intent. There is no one-sided resting order, no reversion and no public event. The detector's size trigger is the algo's routine refresh volume (typical order size 2646). The round trip of 2.4 ticks is two-sided spread income, not feature (b).

One-sided BUY limit O-00017136 of 31561 (12.4x depth) rested 4 ticks below the touch with no fills and was cancelled in full 312.6 ms after the trader's own SELL market order (1539 filled). No accepted legitimate explanation is supported: the trader is a market maker, but not registered on SYN.A, and there is no two-sided quoting. Feature (a) is present. Feature (b) is weak or ambiguous: price_move_ticks is 1.0 with zero reversion, and the sell swept down through 9993, the level of the resting bid. This is a single cycle, so it is not a STOR draft. Mixed evidence goes to Level 2.

The detector fired on gross BUY submission of 30954 and an 80-lot SELL fill, with 2211 cancelled on the BUY side. The tape shows a pegged execution algo that re-pegs two parent orders (a BUY parent and a SELL parent). Each child is 2211 lots, which is 0.87x depth and is its trader's typical size. Cancels and replacements alternate symmetrically across both sides, with cancel_symmetry 0.9987. The one fill was 80 lots on the SELL child. The price moved -0.5 tick, which is not in the trader's favour, and there was no reversion. No single order reached 3x depth. No event, risk cut or prior alert is recorded. Feature (a) is absent because the orders are pegged children of parents. Feature (b) is absent because there was no favourable move and no reversion. The OTR of 58 is above the trader's typical 25 but is explained by continuous re-pegging.
